clue.text: Old man, the Holy One, attends a place of worship

parts.note: an old man is a father, informally pa
the Holy One is God

explanation.surface: An elderly father, a devout man, goes along to a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Buddhist or Hindu temple tower, a building where people worship.

clue.text: Work up energy to jump up and down

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for work reads upwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Getting energised enough to bounce around.
explanation.definitionFit: To pogo is to leap repeatedly on the spot, as punks did when dancing.

clue.text: Flaw showing up, discards various things

indicators.note: showing up in a down clue means the word for flaw reads upwards

parts.note: a bug is a flaw, as in software
to bin something is to discard it

explanation.surface: A defect comes to light and someone throws stuff away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gubbins is British slang for assorted bits and pieces or paraphernalia.

clue.text: Cocktail dress's introduction immaculate, the papers having omitted the last one

indicators.note: introduction picks out the opening letter of the word dress

parts.note: A1 means first-class, perfect, with the 1 written as I

indicators.note: having omitted the last means the final letter of the paper word is dropped

parts.note: a quire is a set of sheets of paper
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A frock's debut is flawless, though the press left something out.
explanation.walkthrough: D begins 'dress'; A1 becomes AI; QUIRE loses its last letter E to give QUIR; then I.
explanation.definitionFit: A daiquiri is a cocktail of rum, lime juice and sugar.

clue.text: Deputy UN Secretary-General, not hot, put on a dinner jacket

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for hot is left out of the Secretary-General's name

parts.note: U Thant of Burma was Secretary-General of the United Nations in the 1960s
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A UN deputy, cooling down, slips into evening dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops the H from U Thant's name; 'put on' is only a link. The surface reads 'UN Secretary-General' as a job title, but it is one particular holder of the post.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is an assistant officer, so a deputy who acts for a superior.

clue.text: Member underlines serious charge, taking Lord's position?

indicators.note: underlines in a down clue puts the limb below the other pieces

parts.note: deep means serious, as in deep trouble
a fine is a monetary charge
a leg is a limb or member

explanation.surface: A limb sits beneath a heavy penalty as a peer is appointed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; deep fine leg is a fielding position there. The question mark flags that a peer's rank is not meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep fine leg is a cricket fielding position near the boundary behind the batsman.

clue.text: Building went up, though not shed

indicators.note: building suggests constructing something new from the letters given

explanation.surface: A building went up, though nobody cried about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a hut beside the building, but it is the past tense of shedding tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwept tears are ones never shed; unwept also means not mourned.

clue.text: Evenly narrated Italian author's style

indicators.note: evenly picks the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of narrated

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: A novelist's way of telling a story at a steady pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: 13 down spin-off

indicators.note: spin-off read as spin suggests the letters of the other show's name are spun

parts.note: the solution to 13 down is the name of the long-running BBC science-fiction show

explanation.surface: A television series derived from another programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Torchwood was a BBC drama derived from the time-travel series, and its name is that show's title rearranged.

clue.text: When short, no longer see how to become a dwarf!

indicators.note: short means the phrase is cut by its final letter

parts.words: no longer see how to become
parts.note: the way to stop seeing is to go blind, read as the phrase go blind

explanation.surface: A riddle about how to shrink into a dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to become no longer seeing' is to GO BLIND; shortening it drops the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a small ugly creature of folklore, like a dwarf or gnome.

clue.text: Spooner says he separates clearish yellow liquids, though this may seem greenish-blue

indicators.note: Spooner says signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: wee is slang for urine, a clearish yellow liquid
a sorter is a man who separates things into groups

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about someone sorting pale liquids, ending on a bluish-green colour.
explanation.walkthrough: WEE SORTER, with the W and S sounds swapped, becomes SEA WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the ocean typically looks blue-green, the shade called sea green.

clue.text: Expression, perhaps too cryptically?

definitions.meaning: an expression such as a metaphor or idiom
the word too sounds like two, a number or figure when spoken, so it is a figure in speech

explanation.surface: A doubt about whether a remark was made too obscurely.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor or simile is an expression using words in a non-literal way.

clue.text: But it should be 'G' for 'Guru', you say, expressed mildly

indicators.note: you say signals that the phrase is pronounced, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the clue corrects an alphabet phrase: a guru is a mystic, so the phrase it objects to is U for mystic

explanation.surface: A pedant complains about a spelling-alphabet entry, put tactfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone has said 'U for mystic'; the objection is that a guru (mystic) begins with G. Spoken, 'U for mystic' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemistic language substitutes gentle words for blunt ones, so it is mildly expressed.

clue.text: Rave about one record following another that is incompatible

indicators.note: following puts the rave-about-record part after the other record

parts.note: another record, here a disc

indicators.note: about means the word for rave goes round the record

parts.note: to rave is to rant
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Ranting about one record after another that doesn't go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the record inside the rave word; 'following' sets that after the other record. 'Rave' looks like a party, but it is the verb to rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrepant means disagreeing or inconsistent, so things that cannot be reconciled.

clue.text: Show, to show how cryptically?

definitions.meaning: doctor how in the sense of rearranging the word how, giving its anagram

explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC science-fiction series is a television show, and doctoring how makes who.

clue.text: Dickens's love for a fool

parts.note: Boz was the pen name Charles Dickens used for his early sketches
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Charles Dickens's sweetheart, offered to a simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: A bozo is an American slang word for a stupid or foolish person.

clue.text: One believing in destiny, rich and very famous

parts.note: fat means rich, as in a fat cheque
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A wealthy superstar who trusts in fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes events are predetermined and cannot be changed.

clue.text: Pressure maintained by runner to get by

indicators.note: maintained by means the pressure letter is held inside the runner

parts.note: Sebastian Coe is a famous British middle-distance runner
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: An athlete keeps up the pressure to scrape through.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage or survive in difficult circumstances, to get by.

clue.text: Bishop on time?

parts.note: a senior churchman, and playfully someone punctual is before being late

explanation.surface: A clergyman who turns up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking churchman such as a bishop.

clue.text: Capitalist side Dali wouldn't have portrayed?

definitions.text: Capitalist side Dali wouldn't have portrayed?

parts.words: Capitalist side Dali wouldn't have portrayed?
parts.note: a football team from the Spanish capital, playfully a side of the capital that the Surrealist painter, who painted the unreal, would not have shown

explanation.surface: A football club seen through the eyes of a Surrealist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalist means from the capital, Madrid; Dali was a Surrealist, so he painted the surreal rather than the real.
explanation.definitionFit: Real Madrid is the famous football club, a sporting side from Spain's capital.

clue.text: Going back the other way, 'e's looking more ill — expecting this?

indicators.note: the other way means the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: 'e's is a dropped-aitch he is, the letters ES
paler means looking more ill

explanation.surface: He looks sicker and fears he may decline again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other way' turns ES + PALER into the answer; 'expecting this?' adds to the picture of a patient worsening.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness or bad habits after improvement.

clue.text: Cyclist possibly taking gamble round fourth of corners

indicators.note: round means the gamble word surrounds the selected letter

parts.note: a wager is a gamble

indicators.note: fourth of picks the fourth letter of corners

explanation.surface: A bike rider takes a risk going round bends.
explanation.walkthrough: The cycle is the Ring cycle of four operas; its composer is a 'cyclist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner composed the Ring cycle of operas, so whimsically he is a cyclist.

clue.text: Unravelling great plot, be in a theatrical scene?

indicators.note: unravelling a plot breaks it apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Untangling a sprawling story to get a part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene is 'theatrical' because surgery takes place in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating table stands in a hospital operating theatre, the setting where surgeons perform.

clue.text: Plant needing a drink

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A thirsty plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Arum is a genus of plants including the cuckoo-pint or lords-and-ladies.

clue.text: No way back after question stands

indicators.note: after places the no-way-back part behind the question

parts.note: what is a question word
taken as written

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for way is turned round

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A refusal to turn back after someone queries a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a stand with open shelves for displaying ornaments.

clue.text: Vicious murderer a wonderful thing

definitions.meaning: a killer who slashes, as Jack the notorious Whitechapel killer was named
a dated British slang term for something excellent, a cracker

explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper was a notorious murderer, and a ripper is also slang for a terrific thing.

clue.text: Single-minded old bag on the shelf

parts.note: a net is a mesh bag
a rack is a frame of shelves

explanation.surface: An elderly handbag left forgotten on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-track mind is obsessed with a single idea, the same as single-minded.

clue.text: Current students

definitions.meaning: a flow of water, like a river's current
a class of pupils grouped by ability in a school

explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flow of water, and in schools a stream is a set of pupils grouped by ability.
